messages.author: b3cdb33506d4db1c
messages.subject: multiple species
parts:
Using DISTANCE is it possible to enter and analyze data from a general
Breeding Bird Survey (Point Transect with two intervals: less than 50 m and
greater than 50 m) in which more than one species may be encountered at each
point?

Avian Ecologist

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: multiple species
parts:
> > Using DISTANCE is it possible to enter and analyze data from a general
> > Breeding Bird Survey (Point Transect with two intervals: less than 50 m and
> > greater than 50 m) in which more than one species may be encountered at each
> > point?

Yes - but you have to supply a nominal maximum distance, e.g. 250m. This
is because Distance evaluates all integrals numerically, so it can't
integrate to infinity. The distance should be a distance beyond which
detections are unlikely - but don't make it excessively large, as Distance
might then fail to converge. You may want to choose a larger value for
larger, more detectable species.

Note that you will only be able to fit one parameter models
(e.g. half-normal without adjustment), and you will have no information to
assess the fit of that model. If you want to do analysis outside
Distance, you'll find formulae on p175 of the distance sampling book
(http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distancebook/).

Handling multiple species is straightforward. Either set up a project per
species, or more simply, create an extra field at the observation level
corresponding to species. Enter a species code in this field for each
detection, then poststratify by species, or select a species at a time in
the data filter.

Steve Buckland
